summary: OptimaThera: multipath fanout caused broker ack backlog, partial transcript loss and billing delta - post-incident follow-up
description:
Issue summary:
OptimaThera (private deployment) experienced a surge of 5xxs and missing transcript fragments between 2026-03-10 01:12 UTC and 2026-03-10 02:04 UTC. Root cause was a multipath fanout change that increased parallel RPCs to the message broker, producing an ack backlog (broker ack debt) which caused the streaming runtime to drop final transcript fragments under load and created a billing delta for retried requests. Impact: customers observed truncated responses and a spike in per-request token billing due to retries and duplicated delivery attempts.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: ~12% of streaming sessions for OptimaThera had missing final chunks (transcript truncation) during the window. Several downstream transcript consumers reported partial messages and duplicate delivery attempts.
- Billing exposure: there was an unplanned increase in billed token counts for OptimaThera due to client retries and server-side duplicate deliveries, estimated ~1.8x baseline token usage for affected sessions during the window.
- Operational: increased broker queue depth and sustained CPU pressure on serving-runtime instances in the private cluster.

Environment:
- Private deployment (OptimaThera-managed VPC) using private control plane, region: us-east-1, cluster: optima-prod-3.2
- Components: serving-runtime v2.18.3, router v1.9.0 (multipath fanout enabled), broker: redwood-eventbus v4.6.1, billing pipeline v1.2.0

Steps to reproduce (investigation procedure):
1) Simulate client fanout: send 50 concurrent streaming sessions with typical OptimaThera prompts and enabled multipath routing to three replicas.
2) Monitor broker ack rate and unacked messages (redwood-eventbus metrics).
3) Observe serving-runtime logs for "final_chunk_dropped" and stream finalization timeouts.
4) Verify billing pipeline duplicates by correlating request_id across ingested tokens.

Observed logs / snippets:
- serving-runtime: "WARN final_chunk_dropped request_id=opt-89ef ctx=stream-finalize reason=broker-ack-timeout"
- broker: "ERROR subscription:ack_debt=312 unacked_messages=1248 ack_latency_ms=1532"
- router: "INFO fanout:parallel=3 route=replica-set-7 latency_p95=420ms"
- billing: "WARN duplicate_token_stream request_id=opt-89ef duplicates=2"

investigation_notes:
Timeline and root cause summary:
- 01:11 UTC: automated rollout enabled router multipath fanout flag cluster-wide for a subset of tenants (canary->gradual).
- 01:12 UTC: OptimaThera private router picked up new config and began parallelizing deliveries to 3 replicas.
- 01:14 UTC: broker redwood-eventbus observed sharp increase in in-flight messages; ack latency rose >1s and unacked message counts climbed.
- 01:20 UTC: serving-runtime began logging final_chunk_dropped events when broker ack did not arrive before stream finalization window. These dropped final chunks caused apparent truncated transcripts.
- Contributing factors:
  * Broker ack debt: the broker lacked tenant-specific flow-control for aggressive multipath; a single tenant’s parallelism could saturate broker IO.
  * Stream finalization timeout: serving-runtime had a fixed short finalization timeout that did not account for transient broker ack latency.
  * Billing pipeline idempotency gap: billing ingestion relied on per-token events without robust de-duplication across rapid retries/duplicates; duplicates were billed before downstream dedupe job completed.

Metrics and dashboards referenced:
- Eventbus: redwood.eventbus.consumer.unacked_messages (spike to 1.2k)
- Router: redwood.router.fanout.parallel (changed 1 -> 3 at 01:12)
- Serving: redwood.serving.final_chunk_dropped.count (12% of active streams during window)
- Billing: billing.tokens.ingested_per_min (2x baseline during incident window)

Temporary mitigation implemented:
- Immediate rollback of multipath fanout for OptimaThera tenant (fanout=1).
- Re-enable broker tenant-level flow-control and reduce per-tenant concurrency.
- Increase serving-runtime finalization timeout by 800ms in the private cluster for affected tenants.

Longer-term remediation planned (tracked in INT-4098):
- Add tenant-scoped broker backpressure and circuit-breaker to prevent single-tenant saturation.
- Implement server-side stream finalization that tolerates broker ack latency via graceful fallback (emit finalization marker and queue late chunk replays).
- Improve billing pipeline dedup stage to perform stronger cross-batch de-duplication before token billing is finalized.
- Add canary gating to router multipath rollouts: require broker ack-rate baseline checks before increasing fanout per tenant.
resolution:
Root cause: router multipath fanout caused an unexpected increase in parallel deliveries to the message broker (ack debt), which delayed broker acks and led serving-runtime to drop final stream chunks under its tight finalization timeout. Duplicate deliveries and client retries led to a billing delta.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: rolled back router fanout for OptimaThera, re-enabled tenant broker flow-control, increased finalization timeout. These steps restored normal ack latency and eliminated transcript truncation by 01:58 UTC.
- Billing: reconciled duplicate-token billing for the incident window (42,000 tokens) and applied a full token credit plus 10% goodwill credit on the affected invoice. Finance approval obtained and customer notified on 2026-03-12.
- Long-term: see INT-4098 for engineering work: tenant-scoped broker guards, improved billing de-duplication, and safer canary gating for multipath rollouts.

Customer outcome: OptimaThera confirmed transcripts are restored and accepted the credits and action plan. Customer rated the follow-up call as satisfactory and will accept closure pending completion of INT-4098 remediation items.

Post-incident things to track (owners):
- INT-4098 (Eng/SRE) - tenant broker guards and router gating - owner: Hannah Kim - target: 2026-04-05
- Billing de-dup (Billing) - owner: Evan Patel - target: 2026-03-29
- Customer follow-up review (Support) - owner: Aisha Carter - target: 2026-03-20
workaround: Applied immediately: revert router fanout to 1 for affected tenant; re-enable and lower broker per-tenant concurrency; temporarily increase serving-runtime finalization timeout for private tenants until code fix deployed.
